newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 23.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page.

WASHINGTON - Four months after President Bill Clinton signed a law barring financial transactions between American corporations and countries accused of supporting terrorism, the administration quietly exempted one such country -- Sudan -- where a U.S. oil company was seeking a stake in a $930 million oil deal.

HAVANA - Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy wound up a two-day visit by announcing a 14-point agreement with Cuba pledging cooperation on human rights and seeking to shield foreign investors targeted for punishment by the United States.
WASHINGTON - An accidental blast near a Planned Parenthood facility in downtown Washington set off a frenzy on the anniversary of the Roe v Wade court ruling on a woman's right to an abortion.
WASHINGTON - In a striking and costly verdict against the use of hidden cameras in television investigations, a North Carolina jury ordered ABC to pay Food Lion more than $5.5 million in damages.

SANTA MONICA - Lacking any motive to kill his ex-wife and her friend, O.J. Simpson has been set up by lying police and slandered by publicity-seeking friends during his civil trial, Simpson's lawyer declared.
WASHINGTON - A vast magnetic cloud erupted from the sun and collided head-on with Earth at one million miles per hour earlier this month, delivering a one-two punch to Earth's magnetic field.
WASHINGTON - As the United States struggles to solve its mathematics problem, it is becoming increasingly clear that time and teaching style appear to be factors.
